title: Sidecar-based conditional metric enrichment for inference KPIs
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
Add a lightweight sidecar that conditionally enriches per-request inference metrics (Prometheus/OTel) with curated labels and trace hooks. Goal is to reduce cardinality and backfill missing contextual labels for custom inference KPIs while preserving fidelity for high-value tenants and models.

Background & motivation:
Current ingest pipeline sees high cardinality from per-request metadata (prompt tags, experiment ids, ephemeral session ids) that pollutes Prometheus rollups and increases storage/cost. Some downstream consumers need contextual labels (model_version, routing_tier, tenant_environment) for SLOs and billing, but we only need them for a subset of requests. A sidecar that applies conditional enrichment and schema validation before OTel/OTLP export will: (1) keep Prometheus time-series cardinality bounded, (2) ensure essential KPIs have consistent labels, (3) attach tracing hooks for causal linking between spans and aggregated metrics.

Goals & success criteria:
- Implement sidecar that intercepts inference host metrics and traces, applies conditional enrichment rules based on sampling policy (deterministic sampling by tenant-model, adaptive by error/latency), and forwards to OTel gateway.
- Reduce top-100 cardinal labels in Prometheus by >= 40% on internal staging workload.
- Ensure zero-loss for high-priority tenants (can opt-in full label set).
- Add trace->metric linking attribute (trace_id and causal_anchor) for correlated SLO debugging.
- Configurable policy stored in ConfigMap/Remote policy service and evaluated in <5ms per request.

Acceptance criteria:
- E2E pipeline test that injects synthetic traffic and asserts expected rollups in staging Prometheus within 5m.
- Unit tests for policy engine, label whitelist/denylist logic, and schema validator.
- Load test demonstrating sidecar adds <3% p95 latency to inference request path and can process 10k metrics/sec per sidecar instance before batching.
- Documentation for ops on enabling per-tenant opt-in and emergency bypass.

Implementation plan (phases):
1) Design: finalize conditional policy language (whitelist, deterministic sample rules, error/latency-triggered enrichment, tenant opt-in). Deliverable: design doc in Confluence.
2) Prototype: build Go sidecar with OTel receiver, simple policy evaluation, in-memory buffer, local backpressure (circuit-breaker) and Prometheus exporter.
3) Integrate: wire to telemetry gateway (ENG-42111) and add trace link attributes.
4) Validation: synthetic traffic tests, cardinality analysis scripts, dashboards updates.
5) Gradual rollout: start with internal tenants, then platform team, then opt-in customers.

Operational details:
- Config: sidecar reads policy from /etc/observability/policy.yaml and fallback to central policy service.
- Metrics emitted: sidecar.enriched_requests_total, sidecar.enrichment_latency_ms_histogram, sidecar.backpressure_events_total, sidecar.schema_rejects_total.
- Tracing hooks: attach attribute metric_anchor.trace_id and metric_anchor.span_index for correlating aggregation windows.
- Failure mode: on policy evaluation error, sidecar falls back to conservative denylist (strip ephemeral labels) and emits alert to Sentry/ops channel.

Testing & rollout plan:
- Unit + integration in CI; e2e harness that pushes 200k synthetic requests, validates histogram stability.
- Canary rollout to 10% of internal infra; monitor top-100 label cardinality and p95 latency.
- Enable tenant opt-in flag and run 2-week pilot with platform team.

Risks & mitigation:
- Risk: incorrect whitelist causes drop of billing labels -> mitigation: opt-in and canary, automated diff check comparing enriched vs raw for opt-in tenants.
- Risk: sidecar becomes bottleneck -> mitigation: autoscale recommendations, increase batching window, fall back to pass-through mode.
- Risk: policy explosion increases complexity -> mitigation: recommend small set of rules and tenant templates, add policy linter (ENG-246801).

Docs & links:
- Confluence design: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Sidecar+Conditional+Enrichment
- Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/observability/metric-cardinality-overview
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/obs-sidecar/pull/312

Next steps:
- Finish design doc review (in-flight, reviewers: Priya Rao, Lucas Kim).
- Merge prototype PR after load test, and coordinate with telemetry gateway owners for integration window.
- Schedule SRE runbook review and postmortem checklist for rollout.
